If the middle of the pill overlaps the camera cutout (always the case in notch mode), long-press a glyph; otherwise long-press anywhere on it, and a long press on the camera cutout hides or shows the pill. In landscape, long-press the collapsed pill.

Tries each Shizuku shortcut the Utilities tab can use (Wi-Fi, mobile data, screen recorder, cache, hotspot) and remembers which ones work on this phone. The others fall back to the system page.

This finds out which Shizuku shortcuts work on your phone. Wi-Fi and mobile data are not switched. The hotspot test turns your hotspot on for a few seconds and then off again. You can skip that test and the hotspot will keep opening its settings page.
Set the camera hole by hand if it is not detected
Use your own area instead of the detected one. This is where the expanded island closes when tapped (portrait). The area never gets wider than the pill\'s centre band.

Last resort when an app shows no download or upload notification (for example its notifications are blocked). Shows an estimated card from overall network speed while the screen is on. It cannot tell which app is transferring.
Hide every event on the lock screen

One choice for the switches below. Calls always show, except with Nothing, which hides the island on the lock screen completely. A mix of your own selects none.
This app\'s cards stay out of the pill while the phone is locked; its notifications are not turned off
Hide per event on the lock screen

Off: no notification cards at all; the notifications stay in the system shade and the island does no work for them
App notifications are switched off, so the notification settings below have no effect until you switch them on.
Off: while the phone is locked only calls open the island by themselves; other events stay in the pill

Pick the system events the cooldown may quiet when they repeat quickly (a charger plugged in again and again, Wi-Fi that keeps reconnecting). The card still shows; only the pop-up is held back. Uses the same trigger count and quiet period as above.

Version, the original project and licences
This app is based on SmartIsland 7.0.0 by Animesh Gupta. The original project is open source; this version changes its animations, layout, settings and features.

Released under the GNU General Public License v3.0. The original copyright notice, Copyright © 2026 Animesh Gupta, is kept as the licence requires.
Lora, Inter Display and Poppins are bundled under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. Fonts you add yourself stay on your device and are covered by their own licences.
How long cards stay and when the island idles
Fine-tune how long things stay on the island. Changes apply straight away and the defaults match the old fixed values.

How long cards stay before the island returns to its idle cutout: ordinary notifications, and live events (music, navigation, timers ...) that appeared by themselves. Live events you open with a tap on the idle cutout stay until you close them. Calls never time out. Slide to the end for Never: cards stay until they are dismissed.
How long Low battery, Battery saver and Fully charged cards stay.
How long a new short event holds the main cutout before the older cards return. It never takes the cutout from a live event.
How long the small round cutout waits, untouched, before it merges into the main one.

A download or upload card the app has not updated for this long is removed from the island. Fixes cards left behind when an app cancels its notification without telling the island. 0 keeps them until the app removes them.
How fast the island opens, closes and moves. Normal is the original feel.
How the small round cutout joins the main one. Slide is the original look; Bubble pushes the two cutouts together, then joins them into one liquid shape.

How far the circle and the bar sit from the side edge of the screen in landscape when they are placed Left or Right (and Camera, when the phone reports no cutout). Raise it to move them toward the middle. It does nothing for Middle.
The white pill at the bottom of an expanded card: pull it down to open the app in a floating window. Off removes the pill, its pull animation and the Floating window swipe action.
Android\'s own freeform windows. Needs freeform support on this ROM (Developer options).
Uses the LMO Freeform app (com.libremobileos.freeform) found on LibreMobileOS-based ROMs. It opens the app\'s main screen in its window.
A small vibration when the island opens, closes, or a swipe action runs. Holding the pill keeps its own stronger pulse.
How easily swipes fire. High needs a shorter swipe. Low needs a longer, straighter one, so a diagonal drag does not trigger the wrong action. Normal is the original feel.
Show the island during Do Not Disturb
Keep showing cards while Do Not Disturb hides notifications. Alert sounds stay muted.
Tapping this app\'s card opens the big card.
Only loud (non-silent) notifications from this app open its card by themselves.
Every new notification from this app opens its card by itself, silent ones too.
Android does not tell other apps which app is using this. Allow Shizuku for Smart Island to list them here.
No app found. It may have stopped just now.
Silent needs Do Not Disturb access. Run the Shizuku setup or allow it in system settings.
The second tab only shows in the island once every cell of the first tab is filled.
Allow Smart Island to modify system settings for this
Background apps stopped and cache cleared
Allow Smart Island to modify system settings to change brightness

Swipe up in the quick-launch window to reach it. The grid is 2 rows of 4 icons: tap an empty cell to add a utility or an app widget, and press and hold an item to drag it to another cell or onto another item to swap them.
Selected. Tap an empty cell to move it there, or tap it again to deselect.
Not chosen yet. You pick one the first time you tap it.
Turn on Floating window in the gesture settings to use this.
Show a small live readout in the collapsed cutout while no event is on the island. Several widgets take turns.
No clock (the status bar has one). On every full hour the hour and the minutes tick over on the cutout, whatever it shows, 12 or 24 hour like the system.
Weekday and day of the month.
Temperature and conditions for your area, refreshed every 30 minutes.
Battery level, green while charging and red when low.
When the next alarm rings. Skipped while no alarm is set.
Live download or upload speed of the whole device.
A glyph ticks in on the left of the cutout at your local 6:00 (sunrise), 12:00 (afternoon), 17:30 (sunset) and 23:00 (midnight). Sunrise and afternoon tick upwards, sunset and midnight downwards.
Unread messages and mail from all your messaging and email apps, as a number on the left of the cutout. Tap it to see how many each app has. Skipped while there are none.

The active mode (Do Not Disturb, Bedtime, Driving, …) as its icon on the left of the cutout. Tap it for the mode\'s name. Skipped while none is on. Grant Do Not Disturb access to tell the modes apart (Android 15 or later).

The mode widget shows Do Not Disturb as it is. To tell Bedtime, Driving and your other modes apart (Android 15 or later) and show their names, allow Smart Island under Do Not Disturb access. It only reads which mode is on; it changes nothing.

Tap a widget\'s icon or value on the collapsed cutout to open it larger. It closes after this time without a touch, or at once with a tap outside it. Its pause button holds the pill on the current widget.
The battery island opens only while charging. It shows the percentage, the time until full, the battery temperature and this value. Wattage depends on the phone reporting its charging current.
The font of the idle widget text on the collapsed pill. The glyphs are white.
Weather needs Network checks, which is off. Turn it on in Notifications and privacy.
Without location access the weather uses your approximate place from your internet connection (wrong while a VPN is on).
Weather uses your approximate location (about 10 km). Only that rounded place is sent to Open-Meteo.
In landscape the idle circle is small, so it shows only the value. Make the circle bigger in the landscape position settings if it is hard to read.
Switches per orientation, which widgets, tick timers
If you close the island with a tap on the cutout, no widget shows when the pill then goes idle. They stay off until you tap to open the island again.
Off after long press to hide
After you hide the pill with a long press, no idle widget shows at all. Showing the pill again brings them back.
These switches are for portrait. Landscape has its own, on the Landscape tab.
These switches are for landscape. Portrait has its own, on the Portrait tab.
Pick any of them. Several take turns in the order shown.
At least one widget stays selected. Switch the widgets off with the main switch.
How often the glyphs on the cutout tick sideways and a faster network speed ticks to its arrow.
How long a widget stays before the glyphs tick away in three steps and the next widget comes in.
Both timers are shared by portrait and landscape.
Everything the island needs to work: restricted settings, accessibility, notification access, hidden notification text, modify system settings, notifications, Bluetooth, battery and background.
The necessary ones plus the optional ones: Do Not Disturb (silent ringer), usage access (recent apps), location (weather, Wi-Fi name) and app-ops watching (privacy dots).
Keep the collapsed cutout the same size when it shows a notification, event or music. Off: it stretches to the size below and shrinks back when the card is put away.
Keep showing music, navigation, timers, recordings and downloads on the island even while their app is open
Every utility cell is taken. Remove one first.
Don\'t show the next alarm on the pill while it is more than 12 hours away.
Current wind speed for your area, with its direction in the island. Uses the same lookup as Weather.
Auto follows your region. Temperature applies to the Weather widget and the battery temperature; wind speed applies to the Wind widget.
Off while a notification is stored
No idle widget shows while the island holds any notification, including ones the idle timeout put away. They come back when none is left.
The glyphs change in short hops on an LED grid instead of one smooth slide.
Numbers from 1 to 9, used in turn and then repeated. 1, 2, 3 means one tick, then two, then three, then round again.
Time between ticks. Lower is faster.
The value steps half a pace after the glyph, like left foot, right foot. A new minute or temperature steps only the value; a new widget steps both.
Letters are drawn as dots. Any font you choose, including fonts you added, is turned into dots.
Applies to the clock, date, weather, wind speed, battery, next alarm and net speed slots. The notification count and mode glyphs keep the smooth tick.
